Background

Practitioner. Researcher. Builder.

In 2013, I walked into the office of the Mayor of Kumasi and told him his revenue collectors were stealing from the city — and that I could stop them with software.

Within three months of deploying the Business and Property Rate Management System, KMA revenue increased by 60%. The Mayor issued a formal commendation and began introducing me to district officials across Ghana.

Over the next decade, I built and maintained eleven production systems across Ghana's core public institutions — pension management, healthcare, banking, education, vehicle licensing, city governance, and marriage registration. These systems serve millions of Ghanaians every day.

I am now applying for a PhD in Computer Science to develop research methodology for AI-driven decision support in civic systems — the exact environments my software has operated in for twelve years.

PhD Research Agenda

Where Practice Meets Research.

01

AI Decision Support for Civic Systems

How can AI-driven decision-support systems be designed for public sector institutions in low-data-literacy, resource-constrained contexts?

02

HCI for Non-Expert Users

What interaction frameworks work for civic workers — hospital clerks, bank officers, pension administrators — making consequential decisions with AI systems?

03

Federated Learning for Government Data

How can disconnected government agencies benefit from shared AI intelligence without centralising sensitive data?
